wowlab {{VERSION}} runs on your own machine against your own World of Warcraft install. It is read-only by default. Every command that changes files asks first and goes through one write gate; a snapshot is taken before the change, and `wowlab undo` reverses it. The only network traffic is fetching public game tables, and nothing is uploaded.

## New in v0.4

- **The game's own files, by id.** `wowlab casc stat --fdid N` says whether one of the game's files is on your computer: local, not in your client's local files (part of this game version, but not on this computer), not among the files your client loads for your language and platform, not part of this game version's files, or encrypted. `wowlab casc cat --fdid N` extracts a local one into wowlab's own data folder, in a folder for this game version, and never overwrites a file it extracted. wowlab never downloads a game file; one that is not on your computer or is encrypted is reported, not extracted. Neither changes anything in your game folder. In `wowlab ui` both are on the Commands tab, and there `casc cat` writes only to its default place.
- **Your character as a 3D model.** `wowlab char model` draws one character from what the lab-addon recorded and the game's own files on your computer: its body, its look from the barber shop, and its gear, as a `.glb` file you can open in any glTF viewer, with its textures beside it as PNG files, in wowlab's own data folder. It says when the gear and the look were recorded, that the model is in its rest pose (the pose stored in the game's model file), and that it is not a picture of how the character looks in game. The first run for a game version downloads the game tables it needs from wago.tools; wowlab never downloads a game file, and one that is not on your computer is left out and listed. Weapons, shields and off-hand items are drawn sheathed on the back or hip, and it says the placement is approximate and not yet confirmed; `--no-held` leaves them out. Nothing in your game folder changes. In `wowlab ui` it is on the Commands tab, and there it writes only to its default place.
- **`wowlab macros fix`.** Where `wowlab macros check` finds a `#showtooltip` (or `#show`) line that is not the first line of a macro, `macros fix` moves it to the top and changes nothing else. It shows the plan and asks first, refuses while the game is running, and takes a snapshot before it writes, so `wowlab undo` puts the old macros back. It fixes your account's macros, or one character's with `--character`. In two tests on one game version, a character's macros changed with the game closed were still there after logging in. Account macros, other game versions, and servers that keep their own copy of your macros were not tested.

- **The crew book, at the desk.** `wowlab crew list` lists the players the lab-addon's crew book keeps for a game account, newest group first, with `--rated`, `--noted`, `--search` and `--sort`; `wowlab crew show` shows everything kept about one. Both only read, as of your last logout or `/reload`, and say so when the book was never turned on (it is off until you turn it on in game with `/wowlab crew on`). Nothing in the crew book is ever sent anywhere.
- **Where the crew book goes with your files.** `wowlab snap export` says when the archive it writes holds the crew book and how many players it keeps ("This archive includes the crew book: on, 3 players."), and the plans of `snap restore`, `undo` and `sv merge` say when they bring it back ("This brings back the crew book: on, 3 players.", or "turned off, 3 players kept"). A book wowlab cannot read is said as such. None of these names a player.

- **Forget, rate and note at the desk.** `wowlab crew forget NAME-REALM` removes one player from the crew book, and `crew forget --all` every player, from `WowLab.lua` and from the game's backup `WowLab.lua.bak`, so the name is in neither file afterwards; whether the book is on stays as it is. `wowlab crew rate NAME-REALM good`, `bad` or `none` and `wowlab crew note NAME-REALM TEXT` make the same changes `/wowlab crew good`, `bad`, `clear` and `note` make in game; a note over 200 bytes, or holding a control character or `|`, is refused rather than cut. Each shows the plan and asks first, refuses while the game is running, and takes a snapshot before it writes, so `wowlab undo` puts back what was there. A forget says what it does not reach: that snapshot and every earlier one still hold the player until you remove them with `wowlab snap rm` and run `wowlab snap gc` (files stored in the last hour stay until a `snap gc` run after that hour), and archives you made with `snap export` keep theirs. `wowlab addon remove` now says that the crew book stays in `WowLab.lua` and that `crew forget --all` empties it.
- **Remove a snapshot.** `wowlab snap rm ID` removes snapshots you no longer want from wowlab's snapshot folder, several at once if you name them; every ID must name a snapshot, or nothing is removed. It shows the plan and asks first, holds the store while it works, and never touches your game folder. The files a snapshot holds stay until `wowlab snap gc` removes the ones no other snapshot needs; `snap gc` keeps files stored in the last hour, says how many it kept, and a run after that hour removes them. A snapshot wowlab took just before one of your changes is refused unless you add `--break-undo`, since the files can then no longer be put back as they were before that change; the plan says what that ends: for your most recent change, `wowlab undo` can no longer reverse it; for an older one, `wowlab undo` is not affected (it only ever reverses your most recent change), and `wowlab snap restore` from that snapshot is no longer possible. It is on the command line only: `wowlab ui` does not offer it.
- **The crew book in `wowlab ui`.** A **Crew** tab beside All characters and Character lists the players the crew book keeps, with a search box, a rating filter and a choice of order; pick a player to see everything kept about them. Rate, note and forget are there too: each shows its plan first and changes nothing until you press **Confirm**, and Confirm is refused if the crew book's files changed after the plan. Names, guilds, notes and instance names are shown exactly as text, never as a link. With the crew book never turned on, the tab says so and how to turn it on in game, and what it would keep.
- **Copy for WoWSims.** `wowlab char sim-export` prints one character as the text WoWSims' Addon Import reads (class, race, level, talents, and each slot's item, enchant and random suffix), to paste into the WoWSims sim for that class; `--out NAME` writes it to a file in wowlab's own data folder instead. Of each item it reads the item, enchant, suffix, gem and bonus fields, and lists what it leaves out (a shirt or tabard, gems, a bonus id that is not one of WoWSims' random suffixes). The talents need one game table, downloaded once with `wowlab db2 fetch TraitNodeEntry`; the export itself fetches nothing and sends nothing. In `wowlab ui`, the Character tab's **Copy for WoWSims** button shows the text with a Copy button. Whether WoWSims imports it is not yet confirmed.
- **Your game's hotfix cache.** wowlab reads the item and talent rows your game keeps in its hotfix cache (`Cache/ADB/<language>/DBCache.bin`, the rows the server has sent your game, at login or when it first showed the item), as your game last saved it, and lays them over the game tables it downloaded, only when the cache is of the same game version. The Twink panel and `char twink` use them and say, for each item, whether its stats came from the downloaded tables or the cache; `char sim-export` uses its talent rows; `wowlab doctor` names the cache's game version and how many rows it adds, replaces and removes, or why it is not used. It only reads the file, never changes it, and never reads the encryption keys the cache also holds. Which of two copies of a row your game shows, and what some of the cache's markers mean, are not yet confirmed.
- **Live, for a second screen.** A **Live** section in `wowlab ui` watches your game folder while you play and refreshes by itself: after a battleground or arena, the match read from the combat log (who you fought, your killing blows and deaths, and the result when the log or the crew book has it); after a `/reload` or logout, your last save, against an earlier one your backups hold (level, gear and currencies from the lab-addon, new items from Syndicator, the matches and the players you met). `wowlab live recap` prints the same. It reads only, and the page asks only wowlab's own local server. A match shows its fights only when the combat log was on during it. The lab-addon turns the log off in instances: to log a battleground, wait for WowLab's chat line that says the combat log is off, then type `/combatlog`, and the game answers that combat is being logged (`/combatlog` switches the log, so typing it while the log is on turns it off).
- **Very large addon files are read in part.** An addon whose TOC file is larger than wowlab reads whole (QuestieDB's is about 19 MB) was left out of `wowlab addons list` and `addons check`. wowlab now reads the lines before its file list (the addon's interface, title, version and the addons it needs) and says, in both commands and on the Addons page, that the rest was not seen.
- **Twink gaps.** `wowlab char twink` lists, for one character and a battleground level bracket (19, 29, 39, 49 or 59; by default the first at or above the character's level), each equipment slot's worn item beside the best items the character could wear there at the bracket's top level, and the gap between them. Items are scored with stat weights per class you can edit (warlock affliction first; `--weights` picks another set, and a `twink.toml` in wowlab's config folder replaces any value), and an item with random suffixes is scored with each suffix. Each item links to its Wowhead page, and the bracket to ForeverTwinking's planner. Where an item comes from is not known yet. The first run for a game version downloads that version's item tables from wago.tools once. Many items are not in those tables: the server sends them to your game itself. wowlab also reads the item rows your game keeps in its hotfix cache (the rows the server has sent your game, at login or when it first showed the item) when the cache is of your game version, and each item says whether its stats came from the downloaded tables or that cache. An item in neither, such as one your game has never shown you, is never a candidate, and a worn one is listed without a score. Armour a class learns later (mail or plate at 40) is left out of the lower brackets, and items only the other side's quests or vendors give are not yet left out. In `wowlab ui`, the Character tab's **Twink** panel has a bracket picker and a weights picker. The stat amounts and the planner's words for classes and races are not yet confirmed.
- **See my look.** In `wowlab ui`, the Character tab has a **See my look** link beside See it dressed, on a character kept only in a backup too. It opens the character on Purist, an outfit builder, with its own face and hair from its last barber-shop visit and its equipped items, in your browser and only when you click it. The address carries the character's name, race, body type, class, barber-shop choices and item ids after a `#`, so the browser does not send them to Purist; wowlab requests nothing. Whether Purist shows every look as the game does is not yet confirmed.

## New in v0.3

- **A new look for `wowlab ui`.** It opens on your characters: one card each, in its class colour, with level, race and class, spec, item level, professions and when you last played it. Above them, two cards: when your UI was last backed up, with **Back up now**, and how many of your addons load on this game version. Everything else is in five sections along the top: Characters, Backups, Addons, Keybinds and Advanced (the file explorer and the other tools from v0.2). Where a figure comes from is one click away, under **About this data**.
- **A page for each character.** Click a card to see its gear in two columns, in item-quality colours, its level and item level over your saves, its professions, each save it has, and a link to see it dressed on Wowhead. Its macros are under Keybinds, below its keys.
- **Names, not numbers.** Races, classes, specs and professions show by name once wowlab has the game's name tables. The first time, the page offers to download them with one button; on the command line it is `wowlab names fetch`. It downloads only the tables that are missing, from wago.tools, and only when you ask.
- **Characters kept in a backup.** A character whose folder is gone from your game (a beta that closed, a folder you deleted) but that one of your backups still holds shows as a dimmed card, "kept in your backup from Oct 19", and opens a page that only reads. On the command line: `wowlab char kept`.
- **No more false alarm about the game's own files.** v0.2 listed some of the game's own saved files, such as the auction house's, as unreadable. They hold an empty slot in a list, which wowlab now reads, keeps exactly as written, and keeps in its place when you merge.

## New in v0.2

- **Every character in one place.** `wowlab ui` lists every character you have played on this computer, in every game version you have installed, as of its last logout: level, class, race, spec, item level, professions and when you last played it. In v0.3 they are the cards on the Characters home; the sortable table is under "All characters as a table". A character with nothing recorded yet says how to fix that. The same table is on the command line as `wowlab char list --summary`.
- **Take a backup now.** **Back up now** on the Characters home saves the game shown at the top; under Backups there is a button for each game version you have installed. Each saves your settings, keybinds, macros, addons and their saved settings into wowlab's own folder, never your game folder. After a patch it tells you the game updated since your last backup, and **Restore this backup…** (under Backups) shows what putting it back would change before anything changes. On the command line it is still `wowlab snap create`, which now backs up every game version you have installed when you do not name one.
- **The patch-day check.** In the Addons section (in v0.2, a card on the Account tab): the addons that are out of date for your game version or missing an addon they need, a count of the ones that are fine, and the saved data that no installed addon claims or that wowlab cannot read. The addon check is also `wowlab addons check`.
- **A character over time.** `wowlab char history` reads your backups back, plus the game's current file: one row per save, with level, item level and spec, and the gear and currencies that changed since the one before. The character page shows the same thing, with a chart of its level. It reads what the lab-addon (`wowlab addon install lab`) records, and the game saves that when you log out or type /reload. History appears once there are two different saves of a character, and the file in the game folder counts as one. So take a backup after you log out or /reload; a backup taken while you are still playing keeps the save from before.
- **The Mac app.** If you would rather not use a terminal, download the Mac app below (see "The Mac app" under Install). It is for Apple silicon. v0.2 and v0.3 also came with a Windows app; Windows is not supported for now, and this release has no Windows app.
- **The package is now called `wowlab`.** v0.1.0 was published as `wowlab-core`. The command is still `wowlab`, and your snapshots, profiles and settings stay where they were. If you installed v0.1.0, run `uv tool uninstall wowlab-core` before you install this one.
- **`wowlab doctor` stays offline.** In v0.1.0, doctor asked wago.tools whether it lists your game version unless you added `--offline`. Now it makes no network request unless you add `--check-builds`.
- **Saved data wowlab cannot read.** `wowlab sv list --unreadable` lists every SavedVariables file wowlab cannot read, for example one cut off during a save, with why, and where reading stopped when it can say. It only reads. `wowlab sv list --orphans` lists the saved data that no installed addon declares, with its size.
- **Move a backup to another computer.** `wowlab snap export` writes one snapshot into a single file, and `wowlab snap import` reads it on the other computer.

## What is in it

It reads an install and tells you what every file is, keeps snapshots of your setup, and puts them back. v0.1.0 was the first public release; this is the whole toolset as of v0.3.

- **Find and explain:** `doctor` (finds the install; a first run says what wowlab will do and offers a first snapshot), `install show`, `tree`, `explain` (what a file is, who writes it, whether it is safe to touch, with the snapshot facts and the commands that read it), `filemap gaps`.
- **The browser view:** `wowlab ui` opens your characters, backups, addons and keybinds in your browser, with the explorer of the whole install under Advanced. It runs the commands that read, and the ones that save only to wowlab's own data (snapshots, profiles, saved looks, the game-table cache, pages), directly. A command that takes `--yes` runs first as a plan that changes nothing, and runs for real only when you press Confirm under it, through the same write gate as on the command line. It listens only on this machine behind a token.
- **Snapshots and undo:** `snap create`, `snap list`, `snap show`, `snap diff`, `snap restore`, `snap verify`, `snap gc`, `snap export` and `snap import` (both v0.2), `undo`.
- **Settings, binds, macros, addons:** `cvar`, `binds`, `binds coach` (from your own combat log: spells cast often on awkward keys, cast with no bind, and binds never used; read-only), `macros list`, `macros check` and `macros fix` (v0.4), `addons`, `addons check` (v0.2), `sv list` (`--orphans` and `--unreadable` in v0.2), `sv dump`, `sv merge`, `addon install lab` (the lab-addon, which records your spellbook, action bars and bindings on logout).
- **Profiles and looks:** `profile save`, `apply`, `list`, `show`, `delete`; `looks import-char`, `options`, `races`, `compare`, `page`.
- **Characters and game data:** `char list` (`--summary` in v0.2), `char show`, `char gear`, `char binds`, `char macros` and `char history` (all four v0.2), `char kept` (v0.3), `db2 builds`, `db2 fetch`, `db2 head`, `names fetch` (v0.3; the one download that shows races, classes, specs and professions by name), `log tail`.
- **For bug reports:** `doctor --redact` prints output with no character, realm, account folder, BattleTag or home path in it; names it cannot find on its own, such as your guild's, go in `--redact-name`.

**Platforms.** macOS is tested by hand on the owner's install. Windows is not supported for now: this release has no Windows app, and the test suite no longer runs on Windows. Linux is untested: CI runs the test suite on Linux, but there is no native Linux client. See the README's platform table before relying on Linux.

**`--json`.** Every read command has a `--json` form backed by a Pydantic model named in its `--help` (`DoctorReport`, `ExplainReport`, `TreeReport`, `SnapListReport`, `SnapRmReport` (v0.4, `snap rm`), `RestoreReport`, `UndoReport`, `CVarListReport`, `CVarGetReport`, `BindsReport`, `BindsCoachReport`, `MacrosReport`, `MacrosCheckReport`, `MacrosFixReport` (v0.4, `macros fix`), `AddonsReport`, `ProfileDeleteReport`, `LookReport`, `LooksOptionsReport`, `LooksRacesReport`, `LooksCompareReport`, `LooksImportReport`, `LooksPageReport`, `CharListReport`, `CharSummaryReport` (v0.2, `char list --summary`), `CharShowReport`, `CharGearReport` (v0.2), `CharBindsReport` (v0.2), `CharMacrosReport` (v0.2), `CharHistoryReport` (v0.2), `CharKeptReport` (v0.3, `char kept`), `BuildsReport`, `FetchReport`, `HeadReport`, `NamesFetchReport` (v0.3, `names fetch`), `LogTailReport` (`LogTailLine` per line with `--follow`), `CascStatReport` (v0.4, `casc stat`), `CascCatReport` (v0.4, `casc ## Install

With [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) installed:

```
{{INSTALL}}
```

Installed v0.1.0 (wowlab-core)? Run `uv tool uninstall wowlab-core` first.

Then run `wowlab --version` and `wowlab doctor`.

## The Mac app (Apple silicon)

No terminal needed: download `wowlab-{{VERSION}}-macos-arm64.zip` below (it is attached a little after the release appears; if it never does, its build failed, so use the install line above), double-click it, drag `wowlab.app` into Applications and open it from there. It is the same wowlab, with its own Python inside, for Macs with Apple silicon; Intel Macs use the install line. It never updates itself.

The app is not signed by an Apple developer account, so macOS refuses it the first time. On macOS 15 (Sequoia) and later, Control-click and Open no longer get past this: click **Done** in the message, open **System Settings → Privacy & Security**, click **Open Anyway** beside the line about `wowlab` and confirm with your password or Touch ID, then open the app again and choose **Open Anyway**. (Not yet confirmed on this app on every macOS version.) A Terminal window then runs `wowlab ui` and your browser opens the explorer; closing the window stops wowlab.

The zip has its line in `SHA256SUMS` and its own attestation: `gh attestation verify wowlab-{{VERSION}}-macos-arm64.zip --repo sandgraal/wowlab --signer-workflow sandgraal/wowlab/.github/workflows/release.yml --source-ref refs/tags/{{TAG}}`.

## Check the download

The `#sha256=` at the end of the install line is the wheel's hash from `SHA256SUMS`, but `uv tool install` does not check it, and checking a file you downloaded says nothing about the copy `uv tool install <address>` downloads again. To install exactly the file you checked:

1. Download the wheel, the sdist and `SHA256SUMS` attached below into one empty folder, and open a terminal there.
2. Check them. Run `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing` (on macOS, `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing`; `--ignore-missing` skips the app's line when you did not download it); each file has to print `OK`. On Windows, run `Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 <file>` in PowerShell for each file and compare the hash with its line in `SHA256SUMS` (the case of the letters does not matter). Then check where the wheel was built: the wheel and the sdist each carry a signed build-provenance attestation. With the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/) run

   ```
   gh attestation verify wowlab-{{VERSION}}-py3-none-any.whl --repo sandgraal/wowlab --signer-workflow sandgraal/wowlab/.github/workflows/release.yml --source-ref refs/tags/{{TAG}}
   ```

   It has to print `Verification succeeded!`; it fails if the file was changed or was built anywhere but wowlab's release workflow from the tag {{TAG}}.
3. Install the file you checked: `uv tool install --python 3.12 ./wowlab-{{VERSION}}-py3-none-any.whl`.

## Changes to `--json` output

Scripts that read `wowlab … --json` depend on the models behind it. Each release lists here every model whose shape changed, what changed, and what a script reading it has to do.

**Since v0.3.0**, every change adds something; nothing was removed or renamed:

- New: `LookupReport` (`lookup --json`): where an item drops or which quest gives it, who sells it, and where an NPC, object or quest is, from the QuestieDB addon installed for the game version (read as data) and the game's item and zone tables: `query`, `kinds`, `flavor`, `version`, `total`, `hits` (each with `kind`, `id`, `name`, `sources` (`questiedb`, `game_table`), the detail of its kind (`item`: `drops` with each NPC, its places, each table's drop `chances`, Questie's `correction`, and `chance` and `chance_from`, the figure Questie shows; `object_drops`, `containers`, `quest_rewards`, `vendors`, `starts_quest`, `given_by_quests`, `related_quests`, `item_level`, `required_level`, `quality`; places carry `own_area` and `estimated`, quests `sort_id`; `npc`: places, `starts`, `ends`; `quest`: givers, finishers, `rewards`; `object`: places, `starts`, `ends`), `heading` and `lines`, the text output's), `questiedb` (`state`: `read`, `not_installed`, `not_baked` or `unreadable`, the TOC read, `tocs` and `chosen_by` when several hold data, `left_out` with each part and why, `unreadable_rows`), `game_tables` (`cached`, `fetched`, `missing`, `error` or `no_version` per table), `words`, `caveat` and `notes`.
- New: `CascStatReport` (`casc stat --json`): where one of the game's files stands in your game version, by its file data id: `state` (`local`, `not_local`, `not_in_build`, `encrypted` or `unknown_id`) with `words`, the same state as the text output says it (for `not_in_build`, one of three wordings), `note`, and for a local file its `size` and `content_key`.
- New: `CascCatReport` (`casc cat --json`): the file extracted, its `path`, `size` and `content_key`, and `outcome`: `written`, or `already_extracted` when the same bytes were already there and nothing was written.
- New: `CharModelReport` (`char model --json`): the `.glb` written (`path`, `outcome`: `written`, `replaced` or `already_there`), its facts, the PNGs beside it, the plan in brief, every model and whether it was placed (`at_origin` when the body model keeps no place for it in the rest pose; for a held item drawn sheathed, `sheathed`, `sheath_point`, `rotation` and `placement`, the words "drawn sheathed, placement approximate (not yet confirmed)", and `sheath_reason` when it could not be), the body texture's painted layers, every file with its state, the files left out, `gear_as_of` and `look_as_of`, `stand_in_look` and `stand_in` (its sentence), `rest_pose` and `likeness`, and the timings.
- New: `CharSimExportReport` (`char sim-export --json`): one character as the JSON WoWSims' Addon Import reads: `sim.text`, the text to paste, `sim.export`, the same object, `sim.left_out`, each thing the record holds that the export does not carry (`what` and `why`), `sim.talents_table_build`, the game version whose talent table was read (null when none was cached), `sim.record_build`, the game version the record was saved by, `sim.note`, the sentence the text output, `--json` and the page share, the WoWSims commit the format was read from, `path`, the file `--out` wrote, or null, and `hotfix_cache`, what your game's hotfix cache did to the talent table (as in `DoctorReport`'s), or null when no table was read.
- New: `CharTwinkReport` (`char twink --json`): the `character`, `file`, `mtime_ns` and `flavor_folder` read, `config_source` (`default` or `user`), `downloaded` (the game tables this run downloaded), and `twink`: the `bracket` and `brackets`, `bracket_from` (`asked`, `level`, `first` or `last`), `level`, `class_file`, `race_id`, `weights_name`, `weight_sets`, `weights` and `weights_source`, `tables_build`, `slots` (each with `slot`, `slot_name`, `worn` (its `score`, or `unscored` and why, `suffix`, `stats`, `required_level`, `above_cap` and `wowhead`), `candidates` (each with `item_id`, `name`, `quality`, `item_level`, `required_level`, `inventory_type`, `two_hand`, `suffix`, `other_suffixes`, `score`, `stats`, `wowhead`, `source` (null: not known yet), `worn`, `binds_on_pickup` and `stats_from` (`game tables` or `hotfix cache`)), `gap` and `gap_words`; a worn item also has `stats_from`, null when it was not found), `planner` or `planner_absent`, the counts `gear_without_details`, `gear_in_item`, `no_level_left_out`, `other_side_left_out` and `by_name_left_out`, `config_file` (where your own `twink.toml` goes), `hotfix_cache` (what your game's hotfix cache did to the item tables, as in `DoctorReport`'s), `words` and `notes`.
- New: `CharLinkListReport` (`char link list --json`): the addresses you pasted for your characters (a ForeverTwinking character page or build, a Warcraft Logs report): `file`, the file in wowlab's data folder they are kept in; `links`, each with `flavor_folder`, `account`, `character`, `site`, `site_name`, `kind` (`profile`, `build` or `report`), `label`, `url` and `saved_at`; `gone`, those of `links` kept for a character folder that is no longer in the game folder (listed without `--character` only); and `refused`, the saved entries that no longer check out, each with `why`.
- New: `CharLinkChangeReport` (`char link set --json`, `char link forget --json`): `dry_run`, `changed`, `plan_lines`, the character (`flavor_folder`, `account`, `character`), `file`, `saved` (the address `set` keeps, as a `links` row), `dropped` (what it replaces, or what `forget` drops) and `links`, the character's addresses after the change.
- `CharTwinkReport` (`char twink --json`): `twink.planner_absent` may now read "<origin> is not a site wowlab links to" when your own `twink.toml` names a planner origin other than ForeverTwinking's.
- `DoctorReport` (`doctor --json`): each of `flavors` gains `hotfix_cache`: null, or what the flavor's hotfix cache does to the game tables wowlab has cached for its version: `file` (relative to the flavor folder), `cache_build`, `tables_build`, `applied`, `refused` (why not, in words) and `tables`, each with `table`, `records`, `added`, `replaced`, `changed` (of the replaced, those whose values differ), `removed` and `left_alone`.
- `CharGearReport` (`char gear --json`) gains `saved_links`, the addresses you pasted for the character, in `CharLinkListReport`'s row shape (empty when there are none), before `flavor_folder`.
- `CharGearReport` (`char gear --json`) gains `purist`, after `saved_links`: the character's look on Purist, an outfit builder, as `{link, site, site_name, label, url, left_out}` (`left_out`: what the address leaves out, in words), or `{link, site, site_name, label, why}` when there is no address. `CharKeptReport` (`char kept --json`) carries it too, as `gear.purist`, for a character kept only in a backup.
- New: `CrewReport` (`crew list --json`): one game account's crew book as of your last logout or `/reload`, and every player wowlab's crew database keeps for it: `state` (`not_turned_on`, `off` or `on`), the game account and flavor folder read, when the book was started, `total`, the `players` shown (filtered and in the order the text lists them), each with its stored `key`, class, level, role, guild, groups shared, first and last group, instance, rating and note, and `in_game_list` (false for a player the game's list no longer holds, whom only the database keeps); `unread`, each entry that could not be read with its key and why; `places`, every game account looked in; `words`, the sentence the text output opens with (the book's state, or that it was never turned on and how to turn it on in game); and `keeps`, what the crew book keeps and where; and `sync`, what the sync into the database run first did (`state`: `synced`, `unchanged`, `held`, `skipped`, `refused`, `elsewhere` or `not_run`, with `words`, `held` reasons, the `plan` (counts added, updated, changed and removed), the `database` file and `left_out`, the entries not synced because they could not be read), null when there was no book to sync.
- New: `CrewShowReport` (`crew show --json`): the same fields for one player, with the name as typed, `lines`, the lines the text output prints, and `sync`.
- New: `CrewSyncReport` (`crew sync --json`): the sync of one game account's crew book into wowlab's crew database: `sync` (as in `CrewReport`; `declined` when a held sync was shown and not confirmed), `adopted` (what `--adopt` moved, null without it), `total`, the players the database keeps, and `words`.
- New: `CrewMatchesReport` (`crew matches --json`): the battlegrounds and arenas wowlab's crew database keeps for one game account's crew book, newest first: `matches`, each with `at`, `map`, `map_id`, `kind` (`bg` or `arena`), `won` (null when the game gave no winner), and the stored keys `team` (with you) and `foes` (against you); with a player named, `typed` and `player` (the stored key) and only their matches; `total`, `words`, `lines` (the lines the text output prints), `places` and `sync` (as in `CrewReport`).
- `CrewReport` (`crew list --json`) and `CrewShowReport` (`crew show --json`): each player gains the record with and against, `allied`, `faced`, `allied_won` and `faced_won` (matches with you and against you, and of each the ones your side won), and the latest match, `pvp_last`, `pvp_map` and `pvp_side`; `CrewReport` gains the filters `faced`, `allied`, `map` and `since`, and `sort` may be `faced` or `allied`; its `sync` gains `matches_left_out`, the matches not synced because they could not be read.
- New: `CrewScanLogReport` (`crew scan-log --json`): one combat log read for the players who fought you in the open world: the game account and flavor folder, `log` (the file read), `characters` (how many of your characters wowlab knows by the game id the lab-addon stored), `scan` (`state`: `scanned`, `unchanged`, `skipped` or `elsewhere`; `how`: `new`, `continued`, `moved` or `restarted`; `read_from` and `read_to`, the offsets read; and counts: `fights`, `outside_world`, `no_zone`, `no_time`, `encounters_added`, `encounters_left_out`, `opponents`, `allies`, `players_added`, `players_left_out`; never a name), `words` and `lines`.
- `CrewReport` (`crew list --json`) and `CrewShowReport` (`crew show --json`): each player gains the open-world record, `world_faced`, `world_allied`, `world_kills`, `world_deaths`, `world_first`, `world_last` and `world_zone`; `CrewReport` gains `world` (`--world`). `CrewMatchesReport` (`crew matches --json`) gains `world` and `encounters` (with `--world`): each with `start`, `end`, `zone`, `instance_id`, `owner_guid`, `died`, and the stored keys `foes`, `allies`, `your_kills` and `killed_you`. `DoctorReport`'s crew databases gain `world_encounters`, `world_opponents` and `world_logs`, counts only.
- New: `CrewEditReport` (`crew forget --json`, `crew rate --json`, `crew note --json`): the change to one game account's crew book: the stored `players` keys it acts on; for `rate` and `note` the `field` with its value `before` and `after`; for `forget`, `backup` (`absent`, `left_alone` or `changed`) and `not_reached`, the sentence on what a forget does not reach; `changed`, `written` and the journal record; and the pin `--expect` takes: `target_sha256` and `written_sha256`, and for `forget` also `backup_sha256` and `backup_written_sha256` (`absent` when there is no backup); and for `forget`, `database_forgotten`, true once the players were removed from wowlab's crew database and its copies.
- New: `LiveRecapReport` (`live recap --json`): for one game account, `match`, the latest battleground or arena the newest combat logs show (`zone`, `instance_id`, `difficulty`, `start`, `end`, `over` and `ended_by` (`left`, `match_end`, `new_log` or null while it goes on), `arena`, `opponents` (each with `key`, `name`, `realm`, `unit_name`, `hits`, `killed_by_you`, `killed_you`), `killing_blows`, `deaths`, `result` (`won`, `lost` or null) and `result_from` (`log` or `crew_book`), `book_map`, `book_foes`, `fights`, `lines`, `logged` and `log_gaps`; `killing_blows` and `deaths` are null when the log was off there; `end` is the match's last line in the log and `end_at_latest` the line that ended it (the next zone line or the newer log's first line), by when it was over at the latest), or null with `match_words`; and `session`, what changed since the save before the newest of one character's lab-addon record (`saved_at_ns`, `since_ns`, `since_snapshot`, `not_compared`, `level_before`, `level_after`, `gear_changes` and `currency_changes` as in `CharHistoryReport`, `new_items` from Syndicator with `items_note`, `matches` and `opponents` since then, `world_note`), or null with `session_words`; `character`, `chosen_by`, `characters`, `logs`, `lines` and `notes`.
- `ExportReport` (`snap export --json`), `RestoreReport` (`snap restore --json`), `UndoReport` (`undo --json`) and `SvMergeReport` (`sv merge --json`) gain `crew_book`: null, or the crew book the archive holds or the plan brings back, as counts only (`paths`, `on`, `readable`, `players`, `unreadable`).
- New: `SpyListReport` (`spy list --json`): what the Spy addon saved, as of your last logout or `/reload`: `files`, every `Spy.lua` looked at (its game account, `character`, Spy's data `version` with any `warning` about it, the `error` when it could not be read, and its counts); `total`, the player rows of the characters listed (one per character that saw a player), and `distinct`, the players among them; the `players` shown, filtered and in the order the text lists them, each with its `key`, `source` (the file, game account, character and flavor folder it came from), the fields Spy saved (class, race, level, guild, faction, `is_enemy` (hostile to your character when Spy last looked), when it last saw them and the place it last recorded, `wins` (your killing blows) and `loses` (the deaths it put on them) when counted, kill-on-sight `reasons`), `kos`, `kos_added`, `ignored` and `other` (every field wowlab does not know, as saved); `kos`, `ignored`, `shared_kos`, `player_notes` and `tags`; `unread`; `warnings`; `caveat`, set when a character listed takes the players other Spy users share; `words`.
- New: `SpyShowReport` (`spy show --json`): the same for one player, with the name as typed, each character's row, their kill-on-sight and ignore entries, `encounters` (the fights Spy counted, each with `time`, `result` and `how`), and `lines`, the lines the text output prints.
- New: `MacrosFixReport` (`macros fix --json`): the macros it fixes, each with its body before and after, the findings it leaves, whether it wrote, the journal record, and `target_sha256` and `fixed_sha256`, the pin `--expect` takes.
- `MacrosCheckReport` (`macros check --json`) and `CharMacrosReport` (`char macros --json`): every finding gains `fixable`, true when `macros fix` corrects it.
- `CharSummaryReport` (`char list --summary --json`) gains `records_in_backups`: folders with no lab record whose record a backup holds.
- `CharKeptRow` gains `folder_present`: true for a character whose folder is still in the game folder but holds no lab record, false when the folder is gone.
- `CharShowReport` (`char show --json`): `record` may be a `CharDBV5`, the lab-addon's schema 5: `macros` (each macro's index, scope, name, icon and body), every binding command as the game returns it, `identity` gains `guid`, `name`, `realm` and `guild`, gear links keep a crafter's GUID, and the record gains `debug`, `announced`, `gathered`, `written_at` and `written_by`; outside a debug session a section of the action bars, bindings, spellbook or macros holds `dropped` and an empty `probes`. A schema 1 to 4 record is unchanged. A script reading `record` should accept schema 5.
- `BindsCoachReport` (`binds coach --json`): `log.counts` gains `by_guid` and `other_guid` when the casts were picked by the character's own GUID (a schema-5 record): `other_guid` counts your casts under another GUID, left out. Without a schema-5 record neither is written.
- `AddonsReport` (`addons list --json`): each TOC's `document` gains `partial`. A TOC larger than wowlab reads whole (1 MiB), which earlier had `document` null and an `error`, now has `error` null and a `document` holding only the lines before its file list, with `partial` true; what it declares after them is not in it. A script that took a null `document` to mean "too large" reads `partial` instead.
- `AddonsCheckReport` (`addons check --json`): each TOC check gains `partial`, true when its fields come from the lines before its file list alone; such a TOC, earlier `interface_status` `unread`, is now judged by those lines.
- `TreeReport` (`tree --json`): the `note` of such a TOC says it was read in part, where it said it was not read.

**From v0.2.1 to v0.3.0**, every change adds something; nothing was removed or renamed:

- New: `CharKeptReport` (`char kept --json`) and `NamesFetchReport` (`names fetch --json`), described below.
- `CharSummaryReport` (`char list --summary --json`) gains `kept_in_backups`, the characters kept only in a backup, and `names_missing`, one entry per game version that has a recorded character and whose name tables are not downloaded, with the command that downloads them.
- `DoctorReport` (`doctor --json`): each flavor gains `names_missing` and `names_command`.
- `SvDumpReport` (`sv dump --json`): an empty slot in a list, which v0.2 refused to read, is now a row whose `value` is `{"type": "nil"}`, at its own `position`.

**Compared with v0.1.0**, every change below adds something: no field was removed or renamed. A few behaviours change, and each one says so below: `explain`'s exit code, `snap create` and `char list` with several game versions, `char list` listing every character folder, `binds coach`'s `chosen_by`, and `looks import-char`'s class. New fields that are often empty are left out of the JSON when empty, so for most installs the output is what it was plus the new fields.

New models, with nothing existing changed:

- `AddonsCheckReport` (`addons check --json`): each addon against this game version, with its interface, dependencies and the characters that have it turned on.
- `CharSummaryReport` (`char list --summary --json`): the Account tab's table, one row per character.
- `CharGearReport` (`char gear --json`): one character's equipped gear slot by slot. Each slot has the item link decoded (`slot_name`, `item_id`, `name`, `colour`, `quality`, `enchant_id`, `gem_ids`, `suffix_id`, `spec_id`, `bonus_ids`, `upgrade`) with `raw_link` beside it. The average item level has `absent`, the reason when there is none. It also has `identity` (described under `CharShowReport`) and `dressing`: either `{url, site, note}`, the address of an outside dressing room (Wowhead's) built from public game ids only, or `{items, note}`, the item ids with the reason there is no address. `wowlab ui`'s Character tab shows the address as a **See it dressed** link, which opens only when you click it; wowlab requests nothing.
- `CharBindsReport` (`char binds --json`): one row per key on one binding command, with the slot it presses, what the lab-addon's record says that slot holds, and which sources have it; plus `left_out_note`, the sentence about bindings the record left out.
- `CharMacrosReport` (`char macros --json`): every account and character macro with its body, where it may sit, and the `macros check` findings for it. `placement.status` is `unconfirmed` or `none`; `confirmed` exists in the model but is not produced yet.
- `CharHistoryReport` (`char history --json`): one character over time, one row per distinct save, oldest first, and the copies that could not be read, with the reason.
- `CharKeptReport` (`char kept --json`): the characters kept only in a backup (their record is no longer in the game folder, but a snapshot of it holds one), as `char list --summary --json` lists them in its new `kept_in_backups`; with `--character`, that character's `gear` (a `CharGearReport`) and `history` (a `CharHistoryReport`) read from the snapshots. Nothing is restored.
- `SnapCreateReport` (`snap create --json` on an install with several game versions and none named). `snap create` used to exit 2 there. It now backs up each one and prints `{"snapshots": [<manifest>, ...]}`. With one game version, or one named, it prints the bare manifest as before.
- `ExportReport` (`snap export --json`) and `ImportReport` (`snap import --json`), for the new commands that move a snapshot to another machine as one file and back.
- `NamesFetchReport` (`names fetch --json`): each flavor folder with its `status`, its version and each name table's status, and how many tables were downloaded. A folder's `status` is `installed`, or `no_version` for a folder with no game version (such as one a beta left behind): it has no tables, nothing is requested for it, and it does not count in the exit code while another folder has a version.

Fields added to existing models:

- `DoctorReport` (`doctor --json`):
  - `wowlab`: which wowlab is running and where it is installed from.
  - `next_steps`: the "Next steps" the text output prints.
  - `build_info_missing`: true when the install has no `.build.info`.
  - `cannot_work_out`: when something failed that wowlab cannot explain, the newest whole snapshot it offers for a restore.
  - `not_taken`: described under `Install` below.
  - Each flavor gains `lab_addon`, the installed lab-addon against this game version.
  - The last-change block gains `flavor_folder`, `snapshot_taken`, `created_dirs`, `temps_removed`, `passed_over` and `paths_left`.
  - The snapshot store block gains `exposure`, which says whether anyone besides you can open the store.
  - Doctor no longer goes online by default. Without `--check-builds`, each flavor's `game_data.status` is `not_checked`. In v0.1.0 that took `--offline`, which is still accepted and does nothing.
- `Install` (`install show --json`), `DoctorReport` and `ExplainReport` gain `not_taken`: for each folder named `_..._` that was not taken as a game version, `{name, reason, target, note}`.
  - `reason` is one of `link`, `no_flavor_info`, `not_checked`, `flavor_info_changed` or `folder_changed`.
  - It is left out when there is no such folder, so most installs print the same JSON as before.
- `ExplainReport` (`explain --json`):
  - `candidates`: for a relative path with nothing on disk and no file-map row, the files whose last parts match it, then the rows that name it.
  - The file-map row and the snapshot facts gain `notes`, `kind` (who took the snapshot) and `newer_pre_write`.
  - **Exit code:** `wowlab explain` now exits 1 for a path that matches nothing; it exited 0 before. A script that runs it on a path that may not exist must allow exit 1.
- `SvDumpReport` is unchanged. `sv dump` now also takes a name as `sv list` lists it: an addon name, a file name, or a path under its account folder. New `--account` and `--character` options pick between files that share a name.
- `TreeReport` and `InstallTreeReport` (`tree --json`): each explained file gains `notes`.
- `Manifest` (`snap create`, `snap show`): `kind`, who took the snapshot: `user`, `first-run`, `profile`, `pre-write` or `imported`. A snapshot taken by v0.1.0 has none.
- `VerifyReport` (`snap verify --json`): `exposure`, as in `doctor`.
- `DiffReport` (`snap diff --json`): `plan_lines`, the text output line by line, with keys, macros and settings by name.
- `RestoreReport` (`snap restore --json`) and `ProfileApplyReport` (`profile apply --json`):
  - `plan_lines`, as in `DiffReport`.
  - `into`, only with `--into-flavor` or `--into-root`: where the snapshot was taken and the account folders mapped.
- `UndoReport` (`undo --json`):
  - `plan_lines`, as in `DiffReport`.
  - `written_paths`, the files the undo wrote.
  - `unlisted_written`, the files it wrote that the plan did not list.
  - `undo --expect <journal id>` undoes only that record; otherwise it exits 3 and undoes nothing.
- `AddonInstallReport` (`addon install --json`): `addon_version`, the version the installed lab-addon's TOC states, which is this wowlab's.
- `AddonInstallReport`, `AddonRemoveReport`, `ProfileApplyReport` and `doctor`'s last-change block: each path left behind gains `exists` and `now`.
- `SvListReport` (`sv list --json`):
  - `orphans`, true with the new `--orphans` (only the files no installed addon declares).
  - `unreadable`, true with the new `--unreadable`.
  - `read_failures`, one per listed file with `--unreadable`: `{path, backup, kind, reason, line, column, detail}`. `kind` is `refused`, with the line and column where reading stopped, `too_large` (not checked) or `not_opened`.
- `SvMergeReport` (`sv merge --json`):
  - `target_sha256`, the target file as the run read it.
  - `merged_sha256`, the bytes the merge writes or would write; null when unresolved conflicts stop it.
  - `removed`, what the merge takes out of the target.
  - `replace`, true with `--replace`.
  - Pass the two hashes back as `sv merge --expect <target_sha256>:<merged_sha256>` to write only if nothing changed in between; otherwise it exits 3 and writes nothing.
- `CharListReport` (`char list --json`):
  - `flavors`, each game version listed with its version and how many character folders it has.
  - `installed_version`.
  - Each character gains `flavor`, `record_schema`, `client_build`, `older_client` and `no_lab_record`.
  - Records skipped as not looked at gain `flavor`.
  - **Behaviour change:** it now lists every character folder, not only those with a lab-addon file. A folder without one has a row with `place` `"no_lab_file"` (a new value), `no_lab_record` saying what its other files hold, and `record`, `summary` and `mtime_ns` null.
  - **Behaviour change:** with several game versions and none named, it lists them all and the top-level `flavor_folder` is null; each row names its own `flavor`.
  - A v0.1.0 script that reads `record` on every row, or treats `flavor_folder` as always a string, needs a change: skip rows whose `place` is `"no_lab_file"`, and allow a null `flavor_folder`.
- `CharShowReport` (`char show --json`):
  - `installed_version`.
  - `older_client`, true when the record was written by an older game version.
  - `lab_addon`, the installed lab-addon against this game version.
  - `identity`, the character's race, body type and class as `{race_id, sex, sex_raw, class_id, class_file}`, each beside its `<field>_absent` reason. A record from an older lab-addon has every value absent: reinstall it with `wowlab addon install lab`, then log in and out.
  - In text, `char show` prints one new `Identity:` line.
- `BindsCoachReport` (`binds coach --json`):
  - **Value change:** `chosen_by` is `"newest schema"` where it was `"latest"`. A script that compared it with `"latest"` should compare with `"newest schema"`.
  - `log.chosen_by` can also be `"caster name"`.
  - New fields: `chosen_because`, `commands_unseen`, `keys_unseen`, `unseen` and `never_cast_withheld`.
  - New in `log`: `character_name`, `casters`, `caster_match`, `warning` and `scan_note`.
  - `log.counts.source_names` and `costs.table.never_cast_min_casts` are also new.
- `LooksImportReport` (`looks import-char --json`):
  - New fields: `class_from`, `recorded_class_id`, `recorded_class_file`, `recorded_class_absent` and `recorded_race_id`.
  - **Value change:** without `--class`, a record that has the character's class now gives the look its `class_id`, where it used to be null. `--class` still wins.
